reason: The exposed ice may need to be chipped to collect a fresh sample, so I will try the geology hammer.
expectation: I expect to expose or break off a piece of ice, though I am unsure whether I need to dig first.

alternatives.reason: A shovel could remove surface material, but the exposed patch suggests a hammer might reach the ice directly.

effect: The hammer produced ice-rich rubble, so I can work on that material next.
reaction: It is satisfying to get material from the exposed bank, though rubble is less clean than I imagined.
reason: The hammer may break the rubble down into a sample I can examine.
expectation: I expect smaller pieces or an exposed interior; I am unsure exactly how it becomes a jarred sample.

alternatives.reason: I could sample the dry bank, but I want to follow the ice first.

effect: The rubble is now a trimmed ice block, ready to put in a jar.
reaction: The progression from rubble to block makes physical sense.
reason: The jars should contain the ice for examination.
expectation: I expect a collected ice sample, perhaps ready for the lens.

effect: The ice is sealed as chips, and the lens is now available to examine it.
reaction: I am slightly surprised the block became chips during sealing, but the sample is ready.
reason: Using the lens on the sealed sample directly addresses the ice examination goal.
expectation: I expect to see details of the ice and perhaps learn what it contains.

alternatives.reason: The dry bank is also part of the investigation, but I want to finish examining the ice first.

effect: The brown line suggests a layer was deposited before later ice, and the next goal is the dry bank.
reaction: I like the small clue to a longer history; it makes the sample feel meaningful.
reason: Sampling the dry bank is the only offered gameplay action and follows the new goal.
expectation: I expect a jar of loose dry material to examine and compare with the ice.

effect: The dry bank sample is collected and can be viewed with the lens.
reason: The lens is the only gameplay option and should reveal details in the sample.
expectation: I expect visible grains or layers, possibly relevant to the ice band.

effect: The dry sample has distinct grains, while the fine brown material in the ice was buried under a later layer; both samples are kept and the ice needs to remain frozen.
reaction: The contrast between the samples is intriguing, though I would like to know more about what the grain differences imply.

mostWorthwhile.text: Seeing the brown band inside the ice was most worthwhile: a physical detail suggested a sequence of deposition and made the sample feel like evidence of a history.

leastWorthwhile.text: Collecting the dry sample was straightforward but had little immediate texture on its own; its interest came only when examined.

surprise.text: The brown line under the ice surface suggested that material had been laid down before the overlying ice, a more interesting clue than simply finding ice.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although trimming a block and then obtaining chips when sealing it was a little abrupt.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue: the layered evidence makes me curious about what further examination could reveal, even though several choices were straightforward.
